tema: From seed to plant: germination and what a seed needs
objetivo: That the student recognizes the parts of a seed, understands that a seed needs water, air and warmth to germinate, and can put the stages from seed to young plant in order.
hatsumon: What does a seed need to become a plant?

turnos.utterance_formal: Good morning, class. Sit down and be quiet, please. Today I have a surprise.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Good mor ning, class. Sit down, uh, quiet please. Today I got a surprise for you.

turnos.utterance_formal: Look at what I have in my hands: a small bag of dry beans.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Look what I have here in my hands, a little bag of dry beans, see?

turnos.utterance_formal: Today we are going to follow a seed from the moment it is a tiny dry thing until it is a plant.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Today we're gonna follow a seed, from when it's a tiny dry little thing, until it's a plant.

turnos.utterance_formal: What does a seed need to become a plant? Think about it while I pass the bag around.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: So, uh, what does a seed need to become a plant? Think about it while I pass the bag around.

turnos.utterance_formal: Careful, do not drop them. Yes, Carlos, you can touch them. They are hard and dry, right?
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Careful, don't drop them! Yes, Carlos, you can touch them. They're hard and dry, right?

operations.text: A dry seed is hard to the touch

turnos.utterance_formal: Raise your hand, please. Soil, says Elena. Sun, says Tomas. Good ideas, we will test them.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Raise your hand! Soil, says Elena. Sun, says Tomas. Good ideas, we'll test them all, okay.

turnos.utterance_formal: First, let us look closely at a seed. Here is one that was soaking overnight.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: First, let's look closely at a seed. This one was soaking, soaking all night.

turnos.utterance_formal: Outside, a seed has a tough skin, the seed coat, that protects it. Inside there is a tiny baby plant and some stored food.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Outside it has a tough skin, the seed coat, that protects it. And inside, a tiny baby plant, and some food saved up.

operations.text: A seed has a **seed coat** that protects it, a tiny baby plant and stored food

turnos.utterance_formal: Who opened the bean? Be gentle. Do you see the little one inside?
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Who opened the bean? Gently, gently. Do you see the little one inside?

turnos.utterance_formal: The skin, the little plant, the food: three parts in every seed.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: The skin, the little plant, the food: three parts in each seed, yeah.

turnos.utterance_formal: Seeds come in many sizes: a bean is big, and a poppy seed is tiny.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Seeds come in all sizes, eh. A bean is big, and a poppy seed is, wow, tiny.

operations.text: Seeds come in many sizes: a bean is big and a poppy seed is tiny.

turnos.utterance_formal: Why does the baby plant need that food? Because it cannot make its own yet. Good thinking, Ana.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Why does the baby plant need that food? Because it can't make its own yet. Good thinking, Ana.

set.text: Seeds come in many sizes: a bean is big and a poppy seed is tiny. Inside every seed, the baby plant lives on stored food until it can make its own.

turnos.utterance_formal: Now your guesses. A seed needs three things to wake up and start growing.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Okay, now your guesses. A seed needs three things to wake up and, and start growing.

operations.text: A seed needs three things to wake up and start growing

turnos.utterance_formal: The first is water. A dry seed is asleep, and water wakes it up.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: The first one is water. A dry seed is sleeping, and the water wakes it up.

turnos.utterance_formal: That is why the seed swells when it is wet, like our soaked beans.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: That's why the seed swells when it's wet, just like our soaked beans, see.

operations.text: A dry seed is asleep, and **water** wakes it up so it swells.

turnos.utterance_formal: The second one is the air, because even a seed breathes, a little.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: The second one is the air, because even the seed breath es, a little bit.

set.text: A dry seed is asleep, and **water** wakes it up so it swells. **Air** is the second need, because even a seed breathes a little.

turnos.utterance_formal: Pedro asks if seeds can breathe underwater. A little air is mixed in the water, but a seed in a puddle for weeks gets too little.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Pedro asks if seeds can breathe underwater. There's some air in the water, but, a seed in a puddle for weeks gets too little.

operations.text: A seed in a puddle for weeks gets too little air.

turnos.utterance_formal: And the third is warmth: not too cold, not too hot.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: And the third is warmth. Not too cold, not too hot.

set.text: A seed in a puddle for weeks gets too little air. The third need is **warmth**, not too cold and not too hot.

turnos.utterance_formal: So water, air and warmth.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: So, water, air, and warmth, yeah.

turnos.utterance_formal: What about the sun, Tomas? Most seeds do not need light to start; they grow in the dark soil.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: What about the sun, Tomas? Most seeds don't need light to start, they grow in the dark soil, under the ground.

operations.text: Most seeds do not need **light** to start growing, because they begin underground.

turnos.utterance_formal: Drinks of water for the whole class? No, I am just kidding. Back to our seeds.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Drinks of water for the whole class? No, no, kidding, kidding! Back to our seeds.

turnos.utterance_formal: Now let us see what happens, step by step. First the seed takes in water and swells. Second, a root grows down. Third, a shoot grows up. And fourth, the leaves open.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Now let's see what happens, step by step. First, the seed soaks up water and swells. Second, a root goes down. Third, a shoot goes up. And fourth, the leaves open.

operations.text:
The seed takes in water and swells
The root grows down
The shoot grows up
The leaves open

turnos.utterance_formal: Say them with me, quietly: swell, root, shoot, leaves.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Say it with me, quietly: swell, root, shoot, leaves.

turnos.utterance_formal: The seed first sends out a root, which holds it in the soil.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: The seed first sends out the, the root, which holds it in the soil.

turnos.utterance_formal: Then the shoot pushes up toward the surface.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Then comes the shoot, pushing up toward the surface.

turnos.utterance_formal: Does the shoot break the soil? Yes, it is small but strong. Look at Marta's face, she cannot believe it.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Does the shoot break the soil? Yes! Small but strong. Look at Marta's face, she can't believe it.

operations.text: The **shoot** is small but strong, and it breaks through the soil.

turnos.utterance_formal: When it reaches the light, the first leaves open.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: When it gets to the light, the first leaves o pen.

turnos.utterance_formal: And, little by little, a young plant.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: And little by little, a young plant, you know.

turnos.utterance_formal: Seed, root, shoot, leaves, plant.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Seed, root, shoot, leaves, and plant.

turnos.utterance_formal: That first stage, when the seed wakes up and the root and shoot appear, has a name: germination.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: That first part, when the seed wakes up and the root and shoot appear, has a name: ger mi nation.

operations.text: The first stage, when the root and shoot appear, is called **germination**

turnos.utterance_formal: When the stored food runs out, the leaves use light to make food for the plant.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: When the stored food runs out, the leaves use the light to make food for the plant, the whole thing.

set.text: The first stage, when the root and shoot appear, is called **germination**, and later the leaves use **light** to make food.

turnos.utterance_formal: Anyone ever planted a bean in cotton at home? Yes, Sofia did. Excellent, then you know this.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Anyone ever put a bean in cotton at home? Yes, Sofia did! Great, then you know all this.

turnos.utterance_formal: This is our experiment. We will put a bean in a jar with wet cotton and wait a few days.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: This is our experiment, okay. We put a bean in a jar with wet cotton and wait a few days.

operations.text: A bean in a jar with wet cotton **sprouts** in a few days

turnos.utterance_formal: We put the jar near the window, where it is warm.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: We put the jar by the window, where it is warm, okay.

set.text: A bean in a jar with wet cotton **sprouts** in a few days, if the jar stays somewhere warm.

turnos.utterance_formal: Who wants to take care of the jar? Everyone? Okay, we will take turns, I will make a chart.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Who wants to take care of the jar? Everybody? Okay, we take turns, I'll make a chart.

turnos.utterance_formal: A second jar will have a dry bean, with no water at all.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: A second jar will have a dry bean, with no water at all, okay.

operations.text: A second jar holds a dry bean with no **water**

turnos.utterance_formal: What do you think will happen to the dry one? Nothing, says Luis. Exactly.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: What do you think will happen to the dry one? Nothing, says Luis. Exactly!

set.text: A second jar holds a dry bean with no **water**, and nothing happens to it

turnos.utterance_formal: The wet one will sprout, and the dry one will stay the same: that shows water matters.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: The wet one will sprout, and the dry one will stay the same, so, we see that water matters.

set.text: A second jar holds a dry bean with no **water**, and nothing happens to it. The wet bean sprouts and the dry one stays the same, so water matters.

turnos.utterance_formal: The wet bean sprouts and the dry bean stays the same.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: The wet bean sprouts and the dry bean stays the same, see, so.

turnos.utterance_formal: We will check the jars every day and see what changes.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: We check the jars every morning, okay, and see what changes.

set.text: A second jar holds a dry bean with no **water**, and nothing happens to it. The wet bean sprouts and the dry one stays the same, so water matters. We check the jars every day.

turnos.utterance_formal: So the answer to our question: a seed needs water, air and warmth, and then it grows a root, a shoot and leaves.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: So the answer to our question is, a seed needs water, air and warm th, and then it grows the root, a shoot and the leaves.

operations.text: A seed needs **water**, air and warmth to germinate, and then grows roots, a shoot and leaves.

turnos.utterance_formal: Water, air and warmth. Those were the three.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Water, air, and warmth. Those were the three, right.

turnos.utterance_formal: Very good. Tomorrow we will look at the jars, so please remember them.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Very good. Tomorrow we check the jars, so remember them, okay.

turnos.utterance_formal: Put your notebooks away and line up for recess.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Put your notebooks away and line up for recess, please.

turnos.utterance_formal: Excellent work today, everyone.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Great job today, everybody!
